source.name: Arrow keys must not select a day that disableDayFn closes, and must stop at maxDate
source.scope: Open upstream bug (https://github.com/Pikaday/Pikaday/issues/955) at 9a90eea5cdbc48784d3a909ddb36e052c16bf25d, unfixed when pinned. Routing Super, then Ultra.

plan.root_cause: The keyboard navigation in Pikaday's _onKeyChange handler uses adjustDate which adds or subtracts days without checking if the resulting date is disabled (e.g., weekends via disableDayFn), allowing ArrowRight to land on a closed day.
plan.repair_strategy: Replace the left/right arrow cases in _onKeyChange with a moveDays helper that steps one day at a time, skipping any dates that are disabled according to opts.minDate, opts.maxDate, opts.disableWeekends, and opts.disableDayFn, while keeping up/down arrow behavior unchanged.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: ArrowRight and ArrowLeft will now move to the next selectable (non‑disabled) day, preventing focus on weekend days and making keyboard date selection usable for users who rely on arrow key navigation.
functional_risks: Performance degradation if many consecutive disabled dates are scanned (mitigated by bounds checks).
If all dates within the min/max range are disabled, the loop will stop at the boundary date.
Up/down arrow navigation still changes the date by exactly 7 days and may land on a disabled day; this existing behavior is left unchanged.
Boundary handling ensures navigation does not exceed minDate or maxDate.
verification_requirements: Starting from Friday 2026-11-20, pressing ArrowRight results in the input value 2026-11-23.
Starting from Monday 2026-11-23, pressing ArrowLeft results in the input value 2026-11-20.
ArrowRight/Left never produce a date that is a weekend or outside the min/max range.
ArrowUp/ArrowDown still change the date by ±7 days.
Manual text entry and mouse selection continue to work as before.
